security_audit.summary: I confirmed the real APIMart network and local token-handling surface in the batch script, while dismissing markdown formatting, file-tree, and high-entropy prose alerts as false positives. No prompt injection attempts or covert data-exfiltration instructions were found. The main residual concerns are single-confirmation API execution and shipping a live env-style config file.

remediation.issue: Batch API execution can proceed after one user selection.
remediation.suggestion: Require a final confirmation immediately before running the APIMart script, and show the endpoint, input file, and output directory.

remediation.issue: The package includes scripts/apimart.env as a live config file.
remediation.suggestion: Replace it with scripts/apimart.env.example, keep TOKEN empty, and ignore scripts/apimart.env in source control.

remediation.issue: API_URL controls where bearer-token requests are sent.
remediation.suggestion: Warn before using a non-default endpoint, or restrict execution to the expected APIMart host unless the user explicitly overrides it.

remediation.issue: run.json can contain submitted prompts and returned image URLs.
remediation.suggestion: Document that output files may contain sensitive prompt content and should not be shared blindly.

semantic_findings.title: Single-Confirmation External API Execution
semantic_findings.description: Stage 4 instructs the agent to generate JSONL and execute batch API generation after the user selects batch API, without a second confirmation. That can send prompt content to APIMart and download remote content, so a final execution confirmation should be required.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The file explicitly says execution happens after one batch API selection and shows the command that runs the APIMart script. The behavior is visible and security-relevant, although it is not covert.

semantic_findings.title: Credential Config File Included in Package
semantic_findings.description: The package includes scripts/apimart.env with a TOKEN field and a comment claiming it contains a real token, although the token is blank. Shipping a live env-style filename increases the chance that future credentials are committed or shared.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The file exists in the package and contains the TOKEN field, but the token value is empty. That supports a hygiene finding rather than evidence of exposed credentials.

content.value_statement: Long articles often produce crowded images and weak prompts. This skill turns content into concise copy specs, layout plans, and reusable image generation prompts.
actual_capabilities: Clarifies content, audience, channel, and text density before planning images.
Breaks long material into a practical image list with one purpose per image.
Creates Copy Specs that define exact on-image text and layout areas.
Packages confirmed copy into 16:9 infographic prompts with style constraints.
Provides reusable templates for covers, comparisons, insight cards, comics, and infographics.
Can prepare APIMart JSONL request packs and run a local batch image script when configured.
limitations: The workflow is primarily written in Chinese and assumes Chinese on-image text.
It does not generate images by itself unless the APIMart script is run with a token.
The default visual system favors 16:9 infographic layouts over photorealistic images.
Batch generation sends prompts and returned image data through the configured APIMart endpoint.

use_cases.title: Turn Articles Into Visual Plans
use_cases.description: Convert a long article into a small set of focused infographic ideas before writing prompts.

use_cases.title: Prepare Course or Workshop Slides
use_cases.description: Create readable cover, roadmap, and explanation prompts for teaching material used on slides.

use_cases.title: Build Consistent Prompt Packs
use_cases.description: Package approved copy, layout rules, and style constraints into repeatable image generation prompts.

prompt_templates.title: Plan One Image
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a single visual.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use image-assistant to turn this content into one 16:9 infographic plan. Ask only for missing audience, channel, and text-density details first.

prompt_templates.title: Split a Long Article
prompt_templates.prompt: Use image-assistant to split this article into a confirmed image list. For each image, give the purpose, content block, and recommended template.

prompt_templates.title: Create Copy Specs
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced copy approval before prompt generation.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use image-assistant stage 3 to create Copy Specs for the confirmed image list. Keep on-image text short and treat it as the final source of truth.

prompt_templates.title: Package Batch Prompts
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced workflow for reusable prompt packs.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use image-assistant stage 4 to turn the approved Copy Specs into prompt packs. Include style constraints, negative constraints, and a manual or batch API option.

output_examples.input: A five-section article about choosing AI tools for a product team.
output_examples.output: A three-image plan with a comparison card, a process comic, and a summary insight card.

output_examples.input: A confirmed slide outline for a workshop introduction.
output_examples.output: A Copy Spec with exact title text, five roadmap labels, and a short bottom takeaway.

output_examples.input: Approved Copy Specs for two social media infographics.
output_examples.output: Two ready-to-copy prompt packs using the same cream paper, colored pencil, and watercolor style.

best_practices: Confirm audience, viewing distance, and text density before asking for final prompts.
Approve the Copy Spec before moving to prompt packaging or batch generation.
Keep one core message per image and use templates to preserve visual consistency.
anti_patterns: Do not put full paragraphs or dense explanations into one image prompt.
Do not change approved on-image text during the prompt packaging stage.
Do not run batch generation without reviewing the endpoint, prompt content, and output location.

faq.question: Does this skill create images directly?
faq.answer: It mainly creates image prompts and request packs. Images are generated only if the local APIMart script is configured and run.

faq.question: Which image format does it target?
faq.answer: The default target is a 16:9 horizontal infographic with large, readable Chinese text.

faq.question: Can I use it for English content?
faq.answer: Yes, but the instructions and examples are optimized for Chinese copy and Chinese text rendering.

faq.question: What is a Copy Spec?
faq.answer: A Copy Spec is the approved source of truth for exact text, layout areas, and text budget.

faq.question: Does it support a consistent visual style?
faq.answer: Yes. It reuses a cream paper, colored pencil, watercolor, and light doodle style block across prompts.

faq.question: What should I check before using batch API generation?
faq.answer: Review the APIMart endpoint, token location, prompt content, output directory, and whether prompt data can leave your workspace.
